claims.text: An Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti multi-principal-element alloy can be selected to form a BCC matrix with L21 precipitates.
The initial cast or powder material may have porosity and a coarse microstructure.
HIP at 1230 °C and 152 MPa for 4 hours can substantially increase alloy hardness.
HIP at the specified conditions will eliminate pores and produce high relative density in the proposed BCC+L21 alloy.
HIP can drive a transition from a single BCC phase to a two-phase microstructure.
Aging for 20 hours at 750–1100 °C will stabilize L21 precipitates in the proposed alloy.
L21 precipitates provide precipitation strengthening in an Al-Cr-Fe-Mn-Ti BCC matrix.
The BCC matrix ensures ductility in the proposed duplex alloy.
The proposed BCC+L21 duplex microstructure will have high thermal stability.
Temperatures around or above 1200 K can produce rapid lattice disorder, incipient melting, and hardness loss.
High grain-boundary density can enhance diffusion paths and promote formation of protective chromia in processed AlCoCrFeNi.
BCC/L21 interfaces facilitate formation of protective chromia or alumina scales.
The proposed processing route will produce relative density above 96%.
The proposed alloy will achieve hardness above 500 HV.
The processed alloy will have lower oxidation mass gain than its as-cast counterpart at 850–1050 °C.
A stable protective surface oxide will maintain aqueous corrosion resistance.
Processing must remain at or below 1200 °C to avoid lattice disorder, melting, and significant hardness loss.
The BCC+L21 design window requires an L21 fraction between 0.05 and 0.5 at both 0.8Tm and 0.5Tm.
Keeping the L21 fraction within the stated window prevents excessive embrittlement.
As-cast or conventionally sintered comparator alloys generally have lower density, coarser microstructures, lower hardness, and poorer oxidation resistance.

contradictions.description: The intervention specifies HIP at 1230 °C, while the boundary says the processing temperature must not exceed 1200 °C.
The mechanism invokes disorder at temperatures above 1200 K, whereas the boundary is stated as 1200 °C or 1473 K. These are different thresholds by 273 °C.
Hardness loss, disorder, or faster oxidation after aging above the proposed temperature boundary would support the claim that the boundary is necessary, not falsify it as the stated rule asserts.
